title: Building on dry land
hookLine: Nuh builds the ark while his people mock him (11:37–38)

lines: A SHIP IN A DRY VALLEY.
cards: A man far from any sea is sawing planks in the sun, day after day. He's building a ship. Not a little boat for a river: a ship, on dry land.
People on their way to the market slow down to stare. Some shake their heads. Some laugh out loud.
A few shout something clever, and their friends laugh too. The Qur'an never says where, so let the scene stay simple: one man, one hammer, and a crowd.

teach.h: BUILD THE SHIP UNDER OUR EYES.
teach.b: Surah eleven. After all those years of calling, God tells Nuh that no more of his people will believe beyond those who already have. Don't grieve over what they do.
Then the instruction, in Pickthall's words: “Build the ship under Our eyes and by Our inspiration.” Under Our eyes: commentators explain it as watched over, guarded, in Our care.
He isn't building alone, even if it looks that way from the road. The next verse brings the crowd.

teach.h: EVERY TIME THEY PASSED, THEY MOCKED.
teach.b: Every time the leaders of his people passed by, they mocked him. The verse doesn't record their jokes, only his answer. Paraphrasing: if you laugh at us now, we'll laugh at you in the same way, and soon you'll know.
It's not a curse. It's a man who's sure of the weather.
Another surah gives a plain detail: the ship was a thing of planks and nails. No miracle wood, just ordinary carpentry, done by hand. When it's finished, the sign comes: the oven gushes.
Commentators differ over what that means, an actual oven, or the face of the earth bursting with water. And God tells him to load a pair of every kind, his family, and those who believe.
Nuh builds before there's a cloud in the sky, because when the rain comes, it's too late to start.
Doing the right thing often looks foolish, right up to the day it doesn't. He didn't need the crowd to understand. He needed the ship to be ready.

how: Muslims read the story of Nuh's ship in surah eleven and elsewhere, and draw from it steadiness in doing right when others mock.

games.q: you're building a ship in a dry valley. the town's leaders walk by laughing. what do you do?
games.why: Nuh answered: laugh now, and soon you'll know. and he kept building.

practice: Sit still and bring to mind one right thing you do that might look odd to others: a prayer at work, a fast, a quiet no. Hold it calmly, and let three words from the verse settle with each breath: under Our eyes.

wordCard.voice: Al-fulk, the ship: what Nuh built under God's eyes, plank by plank on dry land, while his people laughed.

orig.note: Arabic: the ship, the ark; the Qur'an's word for Nuh's vessel in 11:37.

carryVoice: Your line: build before the rain. The ship was ready before the first cloud. Day thirty, done.
